court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: 8th Additional Judge, City Civil Court, Madras, A.S.No.17 of 1994

parties.respondent_defendant: Kuppammal @ Mahamaimary (mother of deceased), State Bank of Tiruvancore, Raja, Stella Nagalingam (legal representatives of the deceased)

facts_of_case: The case is about terminal benefits of a deceased employee Mariaselvam. The plaintiffs claimed as wife and daughter sought for declaration that they alone are the legal heirs and entitled to the death benefit. The first defendant made a rival claim. The trial court declared both parties as legal heirs, but the lower appellate court reversed this decision.

legal_principles.principle: A document may be admissible, but its probative value may still require examination in the facts and circumstances of a particular case.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, a document may be admissible, but as to whether the entry contained therein has any probative value may still be required to be examined in the facts and circumstances of a particular case.
cited_cases: State of Bihar & Ors. v. Radha Krishna Singh & Ors., AIR 1983 SC 684
Ram Prasad Sharma v. State of Bihar, Air 1970 SC 326

legal_principles.principle: The probative value of a document may be nil if it does not disclose the sources of its information or has not achieved sufficient notoriety.
legal_principles.held: The probative value of documents which, however ancient they may be, do not disclose sources of their information or have not achieved sufficient notoriety is precious little.
cited_cases: State of Bihar & Ors. v. Radha Krishna Singh & Ors., AIR 1983 SC 684

outcome.final_order: The final court order directed the second defendant to give employment to the first plaintiff if there is any chance for it.
